chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Mihran, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Muhammad ibn Sinan and Ismail ibn Ibad al-Qasri together, from Dawood al-Raqi who said:

I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): May I be your ransom, I have grown old, so take my hand (and save me) from the Fire. (Who is our companion/leader after you)? He pointed to his son, Abul Hasan (peace be upon him), and said: This is your companion/leader after me.

key_terms.جَعَلۡتُ فَدَاكَ: May I be your ransom (a common honorific address to an Imam)

ai.seo_question: Who did Imam al-Kadhim designate as his successor?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Dawood al-Raqi seeks reassurance of salvation from the aging Imam al-Kadhim, who designates his son Abul Hasan (Imam al-Ridha) as his successor. This explicit pointer (*ishara*) serves as a crucial proof of the Imamate, affirming the continuity of divine authority within the Ahl al-Bayt and establishing Imam al-Ridha as the 'Sahib' (Master/Leader) for the Shia community after him. The designation underscores the theological principle that the Imam is the guarantor of guidance and salvation for his followers.
